title: Harriet Taylor Mill's birth chart
metaDescription: Harriet Taylor Mill's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.3° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Libra — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Uranus. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 14.3° Libra, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Libra (20.6°), Venus in Libra (25.7°), Mars in Sagittarius (0.4°): thought that travels by comparison, attraction that begins as conversation, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars in the same degree of the zodiac from Neptune, 0.2° off exact. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Neptune at 1.9°, and Saturn trine Pluto at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. The Sun in Libra at 14.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; the Moon in Capricorn at 14.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Libra at 25.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 air, 2 fire, 2 water, 1 earth; by modality, 5 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. Venus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.7° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 14.7°.
